notes.title: What Is Going On With Fall Into Insanity?
notes.content:
Hello Everyone, 


I have a few things I would like to say relating to Fall Into Insanity. The news on the game has been very dry since the playtest over a year ago. Well a few things have happened, the first one was the game was internally postponed for reasons I can’t really get into, resulting in lack of updates and news. Today I can say that Fall Into Insanity is in active development once again, although scaled back due to the original idea being overly ambitious. 


[b]How Will The New Version Compare?[/b]

Well the new version of Fall Into Insanity will not feature multiplayer and will be scaled back in terms of story. While the original was primary a story based game, the idea of multiplayer was making it far too ambitious and unsustainable as the ideas kept pilling on. The main story of the original draft got changed several times, for example Croymar Woods, the level you played in the playtest has been completely scrapped. There was ideas for the story involve 5 mini bosses, for example these being the Butcher and Eve along with other characters i didn’t announce. The game would ultimately come down to the main boss who I will not spoil as they will play a huge part in the new story. 

Now the new story is still in progress but it’s not going to be ambitious in terms of features and AAA quality cutscenes. The game itself will push the boundaries as much as one solo dev can do but the gameplay is leaning towards more puzzle like gameplay inspired by many fantastic horror games out there. I am taking great efforts in trying to write and develop a fantastic indie horror game that will satisfy horror fans out there, I’ll be working with more streamers going forward to continue getting feedback and will most likely do another playtest in the future to test out the game again. 


[b]What Engine is Fall Into Insanity Using?[/b]

The game is running on Unreal Engine 5.4, this allows me to push the graphics as much as possible as well as using the new animation technology called Motion Matching which is a powerful tool to make animations smoother and easier to develop as it eliminates having to use state machines to store various animations. With Motion Matching, you load all the animations onto a database and the database decides which animation is best to use for that action. The more animations you add to the database, the better. 


Thank you to everyone who has supported Fall Into Insanity in the past, hopefully I can deliver a product that the horror community will love. I hope to bring you more development updates again soon.

notes.title: The Fall Into Insanity Playtest Has Ended
notes.content:
Hello everyone, The Fall Into Insanity Playtest is over and we hope those who gave the game a try enjoyed their experience. As it was a small slice of the overall experience we are excited to show you more in the future. 

If you haven’t been able to provide feedback yet then please do so in our discord server or the community forums. 

If you would like to stay up to date on news relating to Fall Into Insanity then please follow the game on steam and add it to your wishlist. 



Now that the playtest is over we will get back to work to deliver the game to our vision using some really cool ideas and feedback we have received thus far. We hope to bring you more updates on the game this year, depending on how development goes.

notes.title: Fall Into Insanity Announced, Take Part In The Upcoming Playtest June 27th, 2023
notes.content:
Hello Everyone, we are proud to announce our next game Fall Into Insanity, an atmospheric first-person horror game using Unreal Engine 5. Fall Into Insanity is a single-player experience that follows the player as they look for their friends who went missing under mysterious circumstances in Croymar Woods. 

We are also happy to announce that a playtest for the game will be taking place this month, starting June 27th. The current playtest build features a small slice of the map that will allow us to test out the AI difficulty as well as game performance on various types of hardware. The whole purpose of this playtest is to see how often our AI breaks and if he is very challenging or not. 

The system requirements aren’t final yet but look at the store page to see the minimum specs to run the game and see if you qualify. 

We have been working on this project for a while, we are really trying to make a great game that looks great as well. Hopefully everyone who played our previous game Rent’s Due: The Game will appreciate the jump in graphic power and ambition. 

If you would like to sign up for the playtest you can do so now on the store page. We would also appreciate if you added the game to your wishlist. This will keep you up to date on everything to do with Fall Into Insanity. 

Hope to see everyone on June 27th!
